doc: The shell's and the kernel's commands, by number (@xpute/core/abi/cmd.ts:
`major << 8 | minor`), and the packet each carries — an XTP branch whose
children are listed in order. A command with no children carries no packet.
The same number is a command on the submission ring and a signal on the
completion ring (its `RES` clear). The direction is the ring.

enums.name: Major
doc: What a command is about.

enums.name: InputMinor
doc: The pointer's own verbs, and the map controls'.

enums.name: SensorMinor
doc: The device sensors' own verbs.

enums.name: LoadMinor
doc: A load's own verb.

enums.name: WorldMinor
doc: The world's own verbs.

entries.name: NOP
doc: Replies with its packet's first child, a u32, or 0 — the rings' own
test.

entries.section: the world's turn: the shell's events in, the kernel's asks out

entries.name: WORLD_CREATE
doc: [app_env str, build_time str, build_id str, build_number str, published_tiles bool,
handheld bool, geolocation bool, orientation bool, orientation_permission bool] — the
shell's boot: what the bundler defined and what the device offers; the object store
loaded

entries.name: WORLD_UPDATE
doc: [width f64, height f64, dpr f64, delta_s f64, frame_ms f64, interactive bool,
credits u32] — the
frame of the turn the doorbell's quota rang in: the effects' turn, then the tick's
phases on what is left of the quota, the fetches within the credits; the viewport in
CSS pixels, the frame interval and the turn as the host measured them. The turn
leaves its signals on the completion ring, drawn by the kernel, and last this
command's own as a signal: [draws u32]

entries.name: WORLD_ACTION
doc: [action str (JSON, shell/shell.rs)] — the UI's action; the host rings the doorbell for it at once,
so what it asks of the host is heard before the call returns

entries.name: INPUT_UPDATE
doc: [left f64, top f64, width f64, height f64] — the canvas's client rect

entries.name: INPUT_POINTER
doc: [phase u32 (0 down, 1 move, 2 up, 3 out), kind u32 (0 mouse, 1 touch, 2 pen), id i32,
button i32, x f64, y f64, tool u32 (0 pointer, 1 object, 2 decor, 3 eraser), value u32 (the
placeable cube's or the decor's catalog number), size f64] — a pointer event on the canvas,
in client pixels, with what the pointer holds; the shell sends a move at the last position
when the holding changes, as a browser synthesizes a mouse move

entries.name: INPUT_WHEEL
doc: [delta_y f64]

entries.name: INPUT_TRACKING
doc: [tracking u32 (0 recenter, 1 follow, 2 unfollow)] — the tracking button's press, as
the button showed it

entries.name: SENSOR_UPDATE
doc: [lon f64, lat f64, altitude f64, accuracy f64, heading f64] — a GPS fix; NaN where the
browser gave none

entries.name: SENSOR_ERROR
doc: [code u32 (1 permission denied, 2 position unavailable, 3 timeout, 0 other)] — the
watch failed and was stopped

entries.name: SENSOR_ORIENTATION
doc: [webkit_compass_heading f64, alpha f64, beta f64, gamma f64] — an orientation
event; NaN where the browser gave none

entries.name: SENSOR_PERMISSION
doc: [sensor u32 (0 geolocation, 1 orientation), answer u32 (0 asking, 1 granted, 2 denied,
3 failed)] — a permission as the shell's prompt or the browser's change reported it

entries.name: SENSOR_VISIBILITY
doc: [visible bool] — the tab's visibility; the host rings the doorbell for it at once,
since a hidden page gets no frame and hiding is the save's last sure moment

entries.name: FETCH_UPDATE
doc: [key u64, outcome u32 (0 read, 1 aborted, 2 error, 3 absent), body u32, body_bytes
u32 (0 for none), fail u32, detail u32, net_ms f64] — a read the host finished, its
body held as `body` until the kernel takes it (the `body_read` import).
**Absent is an outcome, not a code the guest reads.** There is no such object,
however the protocol spells that — an HTTP 404, a missing file — and the host is
the one that can tell. `detail` is whatever number the host refused with, kept for
the ledger to print and for nothing to branch on

entries.name: LOAD_UPDATE
doc: [key u64, body u32, bytes u32] — a model's bytes, held by the host as `body` until the
kernel reads them (the `body_read` import)

entries.name: LOAD_IMAGE
doc: [key u64, handle u32] — an image decoded and held by the shell

entries.name: LOAD_DELETE
doc: [key u64] — a read of an asset failed. The guest wants it again, after whatever the
scheduler makes it wait; a model whose *bytes* do not parse is a different thing and
is not this

entries.name: GPU_CREATE
doc: [min_uniform_offset_alignment u32, timestamps bool] — a device answered; the kernel's
renderer is made on it (crates/pxl/web/render/src/gpu/renderer.rs)

entries.name: GPU_DELETE
doc: no packet — the device went away, and every object on it

entries.name: SURFACE_CREATE
doc: tag call · [role u32 (0 world, 1 case)] → result: the surface's handle, 0 refused — a
canvas the shell hands over, drawn by the kernel alone from then on

entries.name: SURFACE_UPDATE
doc: [surface u32, width u32, height u32, device_pixel_ratio f64] — the canvas's layout box in
device pixels, transforms aside; the buffer it is drawn into is the kernel's

entries.name: SURFACE_DELETE
doc: tag call · [surface u32] — the canvas is going; what it held on the device is let go
before the call returns

entries.section: the turn's signals: kernel → shell, left on the completion ring by a strobe or an action

entries.name: WORLD_SNAPSHOT
doc: [at u32, len u32] — shell/shell.rs's snapshot, when it changed: UTF-8
past a ring frame, so it is a block the kernel holds, valid until the
next snapshot

entries.name: SENSOR_CREATE
doc: [sensor u32 (0 geolocation, 1 orientation)] — start watching

entries.name: SENSOR_DELETE
doc: [sensor u32] — stop watching

entries.name: FETCH_CREATE
doc: [key u64, bake u32 (BakeKind), name str] — an object the scheduler wants read.
The guest names it in its own terms — which bake it belongs to, and the name
inside that bake — and the host is the one that knows what address that is and
what protocol reaches it. The key is a handle the shell hands back and never
reads into

entries.name: FETCH_DELETE
doc: [key u64] — stop this read, whichever kind it is. The scheduler took its credit
for something the viewer is more waiting on; the host settles it as stopped, and the
guest still wants it

entries.name: LOAD_CREATE
doc: [key u64, kind u32 (0 glTF, 1 image), load u32 (asset/ingested's asset number, the
texture pack's sheet one past the last)] — an asset the scheduler wants read. It shares
the credits with the pages, and so is started when one is free rather than all at once;
what it is and where it lives is the host's, as a page's address is
